{{Quote|Men of Mandalore! Your chains are gone and freedom is yours&mdash;if you're willing to take it!|Leia Organa|<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />}}
During the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], in the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] and the local [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] fought a decisive '''battle''' in the Mandalorian [[City of Bone]], headquarters of the local Imperial leader, the [[Suprema]]. The battle began in revolt of the Imperial [[Slavery/Legends|slaving]] operation on the planet, when the energy source to the slaves' [[Energy cuffs|energy links]] was destroyed, freeing them and triggering an ensuing uprising.

Although initially meant to be a simple rescue mission of [[Tobbi Dala]], who had been captured by Imperials and detained in the City of Bone, the rescue soon spread to all the Mandalorian slaves in the city. Led by the [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]] [[Fenn Shysa]] and Dala with help from [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] leader [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]], the Mandalorians stormed the Suprema's office to open the [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]] to the city, which had been closed at the beginning of the battle. After overpowering the Suprema, Dala decided to stay behind to open the gates to the city since he had sustained a mortal wound during the struggle.

Aboard a commandeered [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|hovercraft]], Shysa and Organa were able to exit the city to join the freed slaves and Shysa's forces, who had triggered the attack. After their escape, Dala closed the blast doors behind them to stop the pursuing Imperial [[Shrike Squadron (Mandalore)|squadron]]. However, the Imperial [[Starship/Legends|ships]] were unable to change course away from the closing doors and crashed into the walls of the city. As the Imperial craft exploded, they ignited the [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]] in the city, creating a chain reaction that filled the structure with fire, killing all inside.

==Prelude==
{{Quote|We found things had changed durin' our leave. Our homeworld had been overrun by slavers sanctioned by the Empire, an' they'd turned Mandalore into a conscription center fer slaves needed to work the fact'ries, farms an' mines what kept the Imperial war machine runnin'.|Fenn Shysa|<ref name="The Search Begins" />}}
Following the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the emergence of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] from the ashes of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] was in dire straits, having been driven into poverty by siding with the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] during the war. The premier business on the world, [[MandalMotors/Legends|MandalMotors]], who had helped build [[Starship/Legends|starships]] for the Separatists, was subject to a hostile takeover by the Empire, and the board was replaced with Imperial advisers and the lead Imperial adviser, the [[Suprema]], was brought in to round up the populace for [[Slavery/Legends|forced conscription]].<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" /> The slaves were to be subjected to hard labor with the dual purpose of crushing their spirits and using the slave labor to help run [[Mining/Legends|mines]], [[Farm/Legends|farms]], and factories to fund the Imperial war machine.<ref name="The Search Begins" />

The Suprema established his operations in the [[City of Bone]],<ref name="Aliens in the Empire">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/96/indexp2.html|series=Aliens in the Empire|text=Part 1: Hierarchy of Power}}</ref> a massive structure built as a then defunct adventure tourist attraction and made in the image of a 400-meter [[Mythosaur/Legends|Mythosaur]] [[Skeleton/Legends|skeleton]] that resided on the outskirts of Mandalore's [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]], [[Keldabe/Legends|Keldabe]]. Originally sold to the Empire as a local [[Garrison/Legends|garrison]] for [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|credits]] greatly needed by the local Mandalorian clans,<ref name="O66" /> the city became a distribution center for the captured slaves, bound by [[Energy cuffs|energy link]] restraints as they awaited assignment. The Imperial slavers reveled in [[Torture/Legends|torturing]] the hapless slaves, feeding them out of gruel troughs and beating them for even small outbursts.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />

[[File:FennLeia.jpg|thumb|left|250px|Leia Organa overpowers Fenn Shysa, beginning the conflict that would lead to the Battle in the City of Bone.]]
In a few short months, the Suprema had enslaved the majority of the population,<ref name="Aliens in the Empire" /> but he was not without opposition. The [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]], [[Fenn Shysa]] and [[Tobbi Dala]], two of only three survivors of the Mandalorian [[Mission to Norval II|attack]] on [[Norval II]] years prior during the Clone Wars,<ref name="History of the Mandalorians" /> had begun forming an armed guerrilla resistance in the days following the Empire's first arrival on Mandalore, when the [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic]] government had attempted to appear benevolent and their interactions with the Mandalorians over [[Beskar/Legends|''beskar'']] [[Mining/Legends|mining]] operations, legitimate. But once the Empire's grip over their [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] had become strangling, [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] Fenn Shysa and his secret resistance<ref name="O66" /> were labeled as outlaws, though members of the Mandalorian clan-based government decided to secretly help the two [[Soldier/Legends|soldiers]] recruit others and train them to fight against the Imperial authorities.<ref name="History of the Mandalorians" />

Working out of their [[Mandalorian forest encampment|forest headquarters]], the Mandalorian strike force raided slaving convoys, killing the Imperial slavers and freeing their kinsmen. During this long struggle for independence, the Mandalorians were visited by [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] and her [[Protocol droid/Legends|protocol droid]] [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]], who were on a mission to Mandalore in search of the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Dengar/Legends|Dengar]]. Dengar had been rumored to have been working with [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] during the search for the ''Millennium Falcon'' following the [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|Battle of Hoth]]. The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel]] [[Commander/Legends|commander]] hoped that Dengar would lead them to Fett's location, who was in possession of the captured [[Han Solo/Legends|Han Solo]], trapped in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]].<ref name="The Search Begins" />

[[File:BattleCity.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Shysa's Mandalorian forces spy his signal, triggering their attack.]]
Dengar was currently working for the slaving ring<ref name="Aliens in the Empire" /> to capture Fenn Shysa, who was leading the resistance on his own due to Tobbi Dala's capture following a failed mission to the City of Bone. Shysa had actually managed to capture Dengar and was in the process of exchanging the [[Bounty/Legends|bounty]] hunter for Dala during Organa's arrival. However, Organa managed to disrupt the exchange by releasing Dengar and attempting to bring him back to the [[Haven Base|Alliance base]] on [[Arbra/Legends|Arbra]]. The attempt to steal Shysa's prisoner was foiled when Dengar transmitted a message to the Imperial command. Organa and C-3PO were captured and brought back to the City of Bone to be imprisoned alongside Tobbi Dala.<ref name="The Search Begins" />

==The battle==
===Infiltration and revolt===
{{Quote|Hmm, this outlaw assault is rather conveniently timed. And why are they attacking the perimeter when the greatest prizes&mdash;the prisoners&mdash;are inside the skull? Perhaps I'd best take steps&mdash;to assure that they remain inside!|The Suprema ponders the beginning of the assault on his fortress|<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />}}
Undetected by the Imperials, Fenn Shysa infiltrated the city, disguised as a [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtrooper]]. He then freed both Organa and Dala from their imprisonment in the city's detention cells and led them to the [[Hangar/Legends|hangar bay]]. As the group tried to figure out a way to escape from the Imperials, Shysa shot a [[Flare/Legends|flare]] out of a side [[Window/Legends|window]]. Shysa's Mandalorian forces, who were hiding in the woods awaiting his signal, immediately began their attack, firing at the Imperials stationed at the perimeter. The attack was meant to distract the Imperials as Organa, Dala, C-3PO, and Shysa made their escape. However, the Suprema had anticipated the maneuver and ordered the city to be sealed by closing the [[Blast door/Legends|blast doors]].<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />

[[File:BattleCry.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The Mandalorians rise up against the Imperials.]]
At the same time, Dala commandeered a [[Repulsorcraft/Legends|hovercraft]] from Dengar who was in the hangar bay. After tying Dengar up and placing him in the back of the craft, the Rebels made their way for the exit, only to find the doors sealed. The stormtroopers and slaver guards began to fire on the craft, trying to bring it down, since the hovercraft was stranded in the air with nowhere to go. As the Rebels exchanged fire with the Imperials, Organa ordered Shysa to pilot the ship towards the energy link master control, which powered the slave restraints. By concentrating fire on the box, the device was destroyed, freeing the Mandalorian slaves residing in the city. Organa called out to the slaves, encouraging them to rise up against their oppressors.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />

===Assault on the Suprema's office===
{{Quote|You are a man of delusions, Dala. Potentially&mdash;deadly delusions!|Suprema|<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />}}
[[File:DalaSuprema.jpg|thumb|right|70px|Tobbi Dala attempts to attack the Suprema.]]
As a major battle began to erupt in the city, the Rebels took the opportunity to [[Pilot/Legends|pilot]] their craft toward the Suprema's office. The group planned to force the slaver to open the blast doors to let them make their escape. Leaving Dengar tied up in the hovercraft, the group stormed their way to the Suprema's position only to find the door locked. Organa quickly improvised by blowing down the door, but found the Suprema waiting for them with a [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] drawn. Dala attempted to fire on the Imperial slavelord, but was hit in the chest by a blaster shot. As the Suprema attempted to shoot at the rest of the Rebels, Dala threw himself forward, grabbing the Suprema's blaster hand, preventing any further attack.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />

While the Suprema and Dala struggled in the office, Shysa jumped forward, kicking the Suprema and knocking the blaster out of his hand. Distraught over the wound that Dala had sustained, Shysa began to strike the Suprema with the butt of his blaster,<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" /> in an attempt to beat the Imperial officer to [[Death/Legends|death]].<ref name="Aliens in the Empire" /> However, Organa was able to stop Shysa, telling him that they might need the Suprema later. Shysa relented and went to attend to his fallen friend. Unfortunately for the Mandalorian leader, Dala had sustained near fatal injuries, and he bid his friend farewell, promising that he would open the doors to the city. After an emotional goodbye, Organa, C-3PO, and Shysa left both Dala and the wounded Suprema and made their way back to the hovercraft, where Dengar was still tied up.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />

===Escape===
{{Quote|You guys gave us our freedom! An' while most of our lot's escaped, we stayed behind to return the favor!|Former Mandalorian slave|<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />}}
Before the Rebels had broken into the office, the Suprema had been able to get a transmission out to [[Shrike Squadron (Mandalore)|Shrike Squadron]], a flight group made up of [[Imperial escort fighter]]s, who came to the city to quell the uprising. As the Rebels made their way to the exit in their hovercraft, they came under attack by the Shrikes. Although they attempted to return fire, they were outnumbered, and the Imperials threatened to overwhelm them. However, several freed slaves decided to help the Rebels escape. Many of the former Mandalorian slaves were able to escape from the city during the fighting, but those had stayed behind to rescue their liberators.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" /> As the hovercraft passed by, the former slaves threw a gruel trough in the path of the pursuers, knocking one of the Shrikes out of the air and causing it to crash.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" /><ref name="Aliens in the Empire" />

[[File:WallCollision.jpg|thumb|left|210px|Shrike Squadron crashes into the city walls.]]
The diversion allowed the Rebels to make space towards the exit, which had been opened, true to Dala's word. As the craft exited the city, Shrike Squadron converged on the Rebels, continuing their pursuit. However, before they could get to the exit, Dala closed the blast doors. Unable to turn away in time, the [[Airspeeder/Legends|airspeeders]] crashed headlong into the city walls. The massive explosion ignited the [[Fuel/Legends|fuel]] and ammunition within the city, consuming the city in fire and killing all the Imperials inside, including the Suprema and Tobbi Dala. As the hovercraft carrying Dengar and his Rebel captors departed the city back to the Mandalorian camp, they witnessed the destruction, their triumph sobered by the sacrifice of their friend.<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|The attack force got away with light casualties, Fenn&mdash;and most o' the slaves have agreed to join us!|Mandalorian soldier|<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" />}}
Back at the forest base, the Mandalorians celebrated their victory. Many of the former Mandalorian slaves decided to join Shysa's resistance, bolstering their forces. Shysa interrogated Dengar, but he had not actually been Fett's accomplice, only overhearing a conversation that Fett had a secret base in the [[Anga system/Legends|Anga system]]. Although Organa was depressed over not being any closer to finding Solo, she was encouraged by the victory and returned to the Alliance headquarters. Shysa claimed that the attack was not a fatal blow to their enemies,<ref name="Death in the City of Bone" /> but the battle proved more damaging than Shysa had first surmised, and Dala's sacrifice became the pivotal blow in ridding the world of Imperials.<ref name="History of the Mandalorians" />

[[File:BoneExplosion.jpg|thumb|right|170px|The City of Bone is destroyed.]]
Following the battle, Shysa decided to reform his force into the new [[Mandalorian Protectors (Spar)|Mandalorian Protectors]]. Due to Leia Organa's aid in the operation, the Mandalorians joined the Rebel Alliance. Under Shysa, the Protectors began a campaign against [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Miltin Takel]] who oversaw the [[Mandalore sector/Legends|Mandalore sector]].<ref name="History of the Mandalorians" />

==Behind the scenes==
The battle of the City of Bone was the main conflict appearing in [[Star Wars (1977) 69|''Star Wars'' (1977) 69]], written by [[David Michelinie]] and drawn by [[Gene Day]] and [[Tom Palmer]]. Following the end of the battle, Shysa claims that, "the blow [they] dealt the slavers was cripplin' but not final," apparently showing that the battle did not mark the end of the Imperial presence on the planet.

However, the [[2005]] article, [[The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors|''The History of the Mandalorians'']] by [[Abel G. Peña]], claims that Tobbi Dala's sacrifice helped remove the slavers from Mandalore, apparently confirming that the battle was more crippling than Shysa had first presumed. The battle was mentioned once again in the [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] article, ''[[Aliens in the Empire]]'', written by Peña and [[Rich Handley]], when it gave the history of the Suprema who was present and killed during the battle.
